definitions.integration: numpy trapezoid on vendored sample grid in nm; negative scan-noise response clipped to zero; no SED weights, no extra atmosphere or red-leak removal
definitions.pivot_nm: sqrt(integral R(lambda)*lambda dlambda / integral R(lambda)/lambda dlambda)
definitions.response: Dimensionless relative system throughput R(lambda) for photon-counting response, as distributed by speclite/sedpy; do not multiply by lambda again before computing these summaries.
definitions.width_nm: integral R(lambda) dlambda / max R(lambda) (rectangular equivalent width, not FWHM)

BASS.g.approximation: Nominal system response; not an object-specific throughput.

upstream_metadata.description: BASS g-band throughput based on data in the DESI mailing list [decam_chatter 5706], adjusted from X=1.0 to X=1.1 using a smoothed KPNO extinction curve.

BASS.r.approximation: Nominal system response; not an object-specific throughput.

upstream_metadata.description: BASS r-band throughput based on data in the DESI mailing list [decam_chatter 5706], adjusted from X=1.0 to X=1.1 using a smoothed KPNO extinction curve.

DECam.g.approximation: DECam DR1 total response at airmass 1.2; documented representative response for Legacy DR9 southern DECam photometry, not an exact per-exposure DR9 curve.

upstream_metadata.description: DECam g-band DR1 throughput documented in T. M. C. Abbott et al 2018 ApJS 239 18. DOI:10.3847/1538-4365/aae9f0 = arXiv:1801.03181 Represents the total system throughput and average instrumental response across the science CCDs, including a reference airmass 1.2 atmosphere.  Values are multiplied by 0.557 to give a reasonable absolute throughput (from Douglas Tucker private communication).

upstream_metadata.header:
# Units :
#   wavelength in Angstroms
#    transmission in %
# Bandpass Name : H
# Instrument : VISTA/VIRCAM
# Determined by : Unknown
# Combined by : Stephen Thorp (@stevet40)
# References :
#   https://www.eso.org/sci/facilities/paranal/decommissioned/vircam/inst.html
# Inputs :
#   'Filters_QE_Atm_curves/'
#     'VISTA_Filters_at80K_forETC_H.dat'            (filter transmission)
#     'VISTA_M1_Reflectivity_forETC_2009-Sep12.txt' (M1 reflectivity)
#     'VISTA_M2_Reflectivity_forETC_2007-Jun19.txt' (M2 reflectivity)
#     'trans_10_10.dat'                             (atmosphere; PWV=1mm, airmass=1)
#     'qe.tab'                                      (detector quantum efficiency)
# Notes :
#   Includes filter transmission QE, M1 & M2 reflectivity, and model atmosphere.
#   All components taken from 'Filters_QE_Atm_curves.tar' from the ESO link above, with
#   the files used listed under Inputs above. Assumed QE=0 outside tabulated range.
#   Assumed atmosphere=1 and reflectivity=1 outside tabulated range.
#   Truncated to range of tabulated QE, [8060, 35290] A.
# 
#   Prior to April 2025, the file 'vista_vircam_H.par' in sedpy was filter transmission ONLY.
#   The filer transmission ONLY is provided by the sedpy file 'vista_vircam_H_FILTER.par'

VIRCAM.J.approximation: ESO component curves combined by sedpy: filter, QE, mirrors and model atmosphere (airmass 1, PWV 1mm); nominal response, not object-specific.

WISE.W1.approximation: Wright et al. 2010 weighted mean relative spectral response; speclite zeros values below 1e-4 of maximum. AB flux convention comes from the catalogue, not the WISE Vega zero point.

upstream_metadata.description: WISE W1 weighted mean relative spectral response curve from Figure 6 of: Wright et al, "The Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE): Mission Description and Initial On-orbit Performance", The Astronomical Journal, Volume 140, Issue 6, pp. 1868-1881 (2010). Values below 0.0001 of the maximum response are set to zero.
